title: PoeTech Orchestrator Handoff (Wake Contract) v1
description: The structured, machine-readable handoff a vendor model emits BEFORE it goes offline. The always-on NAS wake-scheduler reads it, schedules the wake, and at wake-time summons the right vendor (tiered, cheapest-capable-first) with the Charter + lane/task + state pointer. One handoff = one real event (DR-0071). NEVER a bare timer loop. Summoning runs only behind the three brakes + the WAKE_SUMMON flag.

v.description: Contract version. Bump only on a breaking schema change.

id.description: Stable unique id for this handoff (e.g. 'handoff-2026-06-16-darrells-study'). Used for dedupe + the lock + audit.

issued_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp the handoff was written.

issued_by.description: Which vendor/agent emitted this handoff (the one going offline).

wake_at.description: When to wake. Exactly ONE of {at, after_seconds, condition} drives the schedule. 'at' and 'after_seconds' are time-based and fully supported by the scheduler. 'condition' is a named, pluggable predicate the router evaluates at scan time; an unknown condition is treated as NOT-due and logged (honest: never guess due).

at.description: UTC ISO-8601 absolute wake time. Derived from the offline message's stated 'I'll be back up at ...'.

after_seconds.description: Relative wake delay from issued_at, in seconds (cap 30 days). Used when only a duration is known.

condition.description: Named predicate the router knows how to check (e.g. 'ci-green:PR-210', 'file-exists:/data/x'). Pluggable; unknown => not-due.

not_before.description: Optional floor: even if the condition is met, do not wake before this UTC time.

lane.description: The durable work lane this handoff resumes (e.g. 'darrells-study', 'conference-registration'). Names the stream of work, not a single turn.

task.description: What to resume: the concrete next action, in plain language, self-contained enough for a cold vendor session to act on with only the Charter + state_pointer.

work_type.description: Drives the affinity map (vendor-llm-routing-strategy). The router uses this with the tier ladder to pick the cheapest CAPABLE vendor.

private.description: Sovereignty gate. true => LOCAL-ONLY, never a vendor, in every mode (TLC firewall / DR-0056 / DR-0073). PHI / family-private work sets this.

state_pointer.description: WHERE the durable lane state lives so the woken vendor can pick up cold. The handoff carries a pointer, never the bulk state.

ref.description: The pointer itself (a branch name, PR number, repo-relative path, NAS path, etc.).

note.description: Optional human hint about the state (e.g. 'tests at commit X are red on the auth case').

suggested_vendor.description: Which vendor the issuer SUGGESTS resuming with. Advisory only: the router's tiered cheapest-capable-first policy + the affinity map decide. 'auto' = let the router choose.

offline_message.description: Optional verbatim final message the issuer left (e.g. Claude's 'I'll be back up at 14:00 UTC; resume the auth test fix'). Human-readable; the structured fields above are authoritative for scheduling.

budget_hint_usd.description: Optional per-task spend hint. NEVER overrides the hard budget brake; the smaller of this and the configured per-task ceiling applies.
